title: Doctrine audit across six rule files: two global files contradicted each other, two rules were structurally unfollowable, and the Labyrinth Reflex guard measured the wrong quantity

claims.statement: The two machine-wide doctrine files had overlapping authority and contradicted each other on protocol canon. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md explicitly REJECTED the v15 four-engine model and 5D latent coordinates as undefined and unfalsifiable; ~/.gemini/config/AGENTS.md carried that same model as canon while naming Claude Code in its own audience line.
claims.receipt: Measured 2026-08-08: 21682c vs 27565c, 29 vs 37 headings, exactly ONE shared heading ('## Communication'), difflib SequenceMatcher ratio 0.02. Gemini file contains '### The 4-Engine Knowledge Evolution Architecture & 5D Latent Coordinates' with fixed per-action vectors (Observe [5,0,90,5,0], Plan [30,50,5,5,10]); ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md's v15 evaluation rejects exactly that. Three project files (omission/CLAUDE.md, omission/.agents/AGENTS.md, papers/CLAUDE.md) named the Gemini file 'Global working agreement', pulling the rejected model back into Claude's chain by reference.
claims.note: Resolved by scope, not by deletion: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md gained a 'Doctrine file map and precedence' section naming itself authoritative for Claude sessions and recording the divergence; the Gemini file's audience line dropped Claude Code and now points here; omission and papers pointers were corrected. The Gemini file remains binding for Cursor and Gemini.

claims.statement: Two ALWAYS/NEVER rules were impossible to follow as written and were therefore never followed, which erodes the credibility of the rules beside them.
claims.receipt: (1) 'ALWAYS perform a checkpoint after every four actions' -- a single 2026-08-08 working session made well over 100 tool calls, i.e. 25+ required checkpoints; zero were performed. (2) 'NEVER write, delete, dispatch ... without explicit authority that covers the exact target and operation' -- read literally requires a confirmation before every ordinary file edit, duplicates the harness permission system which already gates this, and contradicts ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md's standing 'reversible + sensible default -> take it, state the assumption, keep moving'.
claims.note: Both rewritten in place to trigger on what they were actually protecting: irreversibility and phase change, rather than an action count; and hard-to-reverse or outward-facing operations, rather than every write.

claims.statement: The Labyrinth Reflex's anti-inflation guard tested confirmed-claim growth, which passes while the graph decays. Nodes written under the reflex are far better evidenced than legacy nodes but nearly twice as likely to be connected to nothing.
claims.receipt: 374-node .lab split by era (dated-2026 filename suffix vs legacy/undated): receipts missing on 'confirmed' nodes -- legacy 167/282 (59%), dated-2026 2/58 (3%). Isolated (degree 0) -- legacy 33/284 (12%), dated-2026 18/87 (21%). 49 nodes created in the first 8 days of August. Confirmed claims WERE growing; edges were not.
claims.note: Guard retargeted to isolated-node fraction and edges-per-node, with an instruction to name what a new node attaches to before writing it. The receipt discipline this reflex produced is genuinely excellent and was left alone.

claims.statement: Two rules in the same file gave opposite defaults for creating files, with no stated boundary: 'prefer editing existing files over creating new ones' versus 'never overwrite a source document in place; write a new file and preserve the original'.
claims.receipt: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, Scope discipline vs Working with Documents. Friction observed the same day: creating jnwb/paths.py and a new SKILL.md each required arguing against the first rule despite both being correct.
claims.note: Resolved with a scope line -- code prefers editing in place (versioned, diffable, recoverable); documents, manuscripts, and analysis outputs prefer a new file with the original preserved.

claims.statement: Stating GLMM as the unconditional default created naming pressure that produced a documented mislabel in this repo.
claims.receipt: context/figures/fig04_omission_identity_decoding/README.md item 2: omission_identity_glmm_coefficients.csv and Panel D's title call the model a GLMM; the actual fit is one sklearn LogisticRegression(C=1.0, penalty='l2') with no random-effects structure whatsoever.
claims.note: Clause added: GLMM is the default only when the design supports a variance component, and a model with no random effects is not a GLMM however it is titled.

claims.statement: Global doctrine carried nothing on signal processing, array backends, biophysical modelling, or scientific writing, despite those being the substance of the work. JAX in particular was absent from doctrine while being the dominant stack in one repo.
claims.receipt: Import census: jaxfne -- jax 311 sites, numpy 176, jaxley 8, scipy 5. omission -- numpy 86, pandas 75, sklearn 59, scipy 24, statsmodels 17, plus torch and cupy. ~/.claude/skills/ did not exist, so NO user-scope skill loaded in jaxfne or papers at all.
claims.note: Four skills created at user scope (signal-processing, numerical-computing, biophysical-modeling, scientific-writing) plus short directive blocks in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for the rules that must fire BEFORE code is written. numerical-computing was moved from omission project scope to user scope and generalized, since jaxfne needs it more.

claims.statement: The always-loaded cost of this change was estimated at ~1,500 chars in the proposal and delivered 8,192 -- a 5x miss on my own estimate, which the user approved on the basis of the smaller number.
claims.receipt: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md 21682c -> 29874c (+8192c, ~+2048 est. tokens, loaded in EVERY project). Breakdown: doctrine precedence section 1970c, signal processing 1349c, biophysical 1248c, scientific writing 1077c, array backends 810c, in-place rule fixes 1738c. Still under the ~40000c large-file warning threshold. Skill listing in omission hit 2043 tok against a ~2000 budget and was brought to 1873 tok by tightening the four new descriptions.
claims.note: Stated because the approval rested on the smaller figure. The content is defensible -- directives that must load before code is written cannot live behind lazy invocation -- but the estimate was wrong and the user should decide whether to trim.

issues: The four new skills were written from doctrine and general knowledge, not from doing the work they describe. The signal-processing dB-order claim and the fig04 GLMM mislabel are measured on this corpus; the biophysical-modeling and neuropsychology sections are asserted from general knowledge and have no receipt from these repos.
omission/.agents/AGENTS.md (28,020c) still names the Gemini file as global agreement and was NOT edited this pass -- only omission/CLAUDE.md and papers/CLAUDE.md pointers were corrected.
jaxfne/AGENTS.md was inventoried but not edited; it has its own 'Truth gates' and 'Labyrinth is not optional' sections that were not audited against the corrected global doctrine.

papers/CLAUDE.md points at ~/.gemini/config/skills/labyrinth-protocol/SKILL.md as 'canonical protocol' -- a FOURTH copy of the Labyrinth rules, which exists on disk but was not diffed against the other three.
Backups of all four edited doctrine files are at ~/.claude/backups/doctrine-20260808/ -- Conservation holds, every edit is revertible.
falsifier: Closed when a future session in jaxfne or papers loads the user-scope skills and the corrected precedence without re-deriving any of it, and when a graph-health re-run shows the isolated-node fraction for newly written nodes falling below the 12% legacy baseline rather than sitting at 21%.
